tldr: BehaviorGPT is a fully autoregressive Transformer with only 3M parameters that simulates multi-agent traffic behavior using a Next-Patch Prediction Paradigm (NP3), winning first place in the 2024 Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge.
contributions: A fully autoregressive homogeneous Transformer architecture for smart agent simulation that eliminates the traditional encoder-decoder separation between history and future
The Next-Patch Prediction Paradigm (NP3) that prevents trivial shortcuts by training models to reason at the patch level and capture long-range spatial-temporal interactions
First-place performance in the 2024 Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge with a realism score of 0.7473 and minADE of 1.4147 using only 3M parameters
methods: BehaviorGPT uses a fully autoregressive Transformer decoder with homogeneous blocks to process multi-agent trajectory sequences without separating history from future. Each time step is treated as 'current' for motion generation, maximizing data utilization. The model employs a Next-Patch Prediction Paradigm (NP3) where it autoregressively generates trajectory patches containing multiple time steps. It uses relative spacetime representations to symmetrically model patches in space and time, with a triple-attention mechanism comprising temporal self-attention, agent-map cross-attention (with k-NN filtering), and agent-agent self-attention (also with k-NN filtering). The prediction head uses a GRU-based autoregressive RNN to unroll states within each patch, modeling position and velocity as Laplace distributions and yaw as a von Mises distribution across multiple modes.
results: BehaviorGPT won first place in the 2024 Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge with merely 3M parameters, achieving a realism score of 0.7473 and a minADE score of 1.4147, demonstrating superior performance in traffic agent simulation.
limitations: The paper notes that naive next-token prediction in autoregressive modeling suffers from compounding errors and causal confusion. Blindsly copying LLM next-token prediction could allow models to achieve low training loss by simply copying the current token as the next one without performing long-range interaction reasoning—addressed by NP3 but not explicitly quantified. The assumption that agents plan motions independently within a patch horizon (Eq. 3) may not capture all inter-agent dependencies.
